rationale: The rotating-plate idea is most legible in the top view, but the isometric and front views read primarily as a low pile of thin, overlapping slabs rather than a unified torqued stack around a stabilizing core. The candidate avoids conventional stair-step massing, yet lacks a strong primary volume and a clearly formed public void. Several plates appear to collide or over-clip at their intersections, weakening coherence across views. The shifted-platform and torque references are present as abstract signals, but the massing does not yet achieve their disciplined hierarchy.
warnings: The dominant gesture is not consistently legible across all four views.
The top view shows ambiguous overlaps and possible solid collisions.
The claimed stabilizing core is not visually strong enough to organize the plates.
The court or undercroft is not clearly defined as a meaningful open void.
